## Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar is the settlement layer for the approved operation. Buyer approval binds the complete request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. The native Stellar SDK and configured payment service verify and settle the authorization; the application connects that outcome to the original source, useful result and merchant fulfillment. Buyers control signing and aggregate spending. Merchants control their resources, terms and order actions.

We compose existing ecosystem infrastructure. The x402 Exact Stellar scheme and facilitator supply payment verification and settlement. Vellar’s optional discovery extension publishes eligible settled resources to its catalogue. OpenZeppelin, Veridex and Periplo supply relevant payment infrastructure; Rumble Fish is developing facilitator, discovery and SDK capabilities. Our existing MPP Charge workbench retains that protocol’s own challenge, authorization and recovery model. We use the existing SDK and token contracts.

Our contribution is the repeated source-to-customer operation around those components: preserve the source’s types and pagination; review the exact request and terms; acquire the complete result; receive it into an existing application, report or workbook; and reopen the operating state after interruption or on another authorized host. This gives Stellar merchants a reusable path from a paid endpoint to an independently maintainable customer installation.

A retained comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity. The two-facilitator milestone therefore includes the actual registration and integration work for the same useful service. Its completion will demonstrate that a merchant can change payment infrastructure while preserving the customer operation. Reusable integration, receiving and operating improvements will return to the public source.

## Defined architecture and operating behavior

The system has six components: the merchant’s private source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the native Stellar SDK and selected facilitator; the buyer’s private approval and spending state; complete result and delivery records; and merchant fulfillment/accounting. Node.js supplies the merchant and buyer interfaces. Source adapters and customer applications retain their own native data and operating semantics.

|Stage|Implemented behavior|
|  ---  |  ---  |
|Review and publish|The merchant selects a source edition or named live query, request schema, public output, limits and resolved payment options. It reviews rights, route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Later source or terms changes become reviewed states.|
|Connect the source|Adapters preserve types, missing and null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select authorized access. The output identifies its source edition.|
|Approve and purchase|The buyer retains the endpoint, method or MCP tool, arguments, selected terms and scope. The remote schema and challenge must match before signing. Per-payment limits and the application’s existing reservation/budget owner govern spend.|
|Settle and deliver|The facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. The application retains the server outcome, complete output and durable merchant notification. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the transaction’s network, asset, parties and atomic amount.|
|Use and continue|The receiving application opens all pages and files required by the agreed task. Its parent acquisition retains the paid requests and incomplete coverage. Earlier acquired output remains available when a later source edition changes.|
|Operate and hand over|The customer selects its release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. A receiving engineer can drain, restart, roll back and restore it with the original operating history and complete customer files.|


For paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments remain distinct from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge. Its full payment option, including authorization timeout, must match the saved quote before the buyer retains dispatch state and sends the signed tool call. The official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata; HTTP operations use the native HTTP transport.

Recovery keeps server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete output, receiver acknowledgment and fulfillment separately visible. An uncertain signed response retains its original dispatch state for reconciliation. Reopening an acquired result uses the saved work; an unfinished delivery continues from its original intent. A changed request or new purchase receives a new review. Export and restore carry the configuration selection, history and complete referenced files, while the receiving host supplies current authorized secret references.

The same workspaces are available through the browser, terminal, typed clients and MCP. The captured-API product connects reusable route policies to a saved operator procedure, exact native configuration review, continued publication and complete customer files. Its collaboration workflow supports independent draft edits, explicit resolution of overlapping changes and portable working-edit files. The original draft and package writers retain the save, export and receiving lifecycle. This supports installation work by multiple operators while preserving the selected source, procedures and earlier decisions.

## 7. Threat response and useful-outcome measurement

T2 includes the actual deployment's threat assessment, monitoring thresholds, notification destinations, accountable responders and material remediation.

| Failure to operate | Control and observation |
| --- | --- |
| Changed source, request or terms | Match exact source generation, request and approved payment alternative before dispatch. Retain rejection cause, quote age, source expiry and capacity refusal. |
| Uncertain payment or incomplete delivery | Reconcile the original intent and transfer, retain partial output/entitlement state and recover unfinished work. Measure outstanding age and time to useful output. |
| Unauthorized access or exposed private state | Validate issuer, audience, subject, scopes, expiry and current authority. Restrict administration and protect credentials, keys, claim tokens, private bodies and backups; retain access/rotation observations. |
| Observation or notification failure | Keep the last useful capture, incident and original notification attempts. Retry the same event; measure coverage, alert, acknowledgment and recovery time. |
| Restart or state loss | Restore the selected backup and reconcile later operations. Reopen the same support case and full output on the receiving host; measure time, retained history and active effort. |

Count each independent organization or person once across agents and wallets. A completed purchase joins one distinct approved intent, an independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Transactions are deduplicated within their network; amounts and fees retain their asset and atomic units. Required fulfillment remains separately visible.

Report completed/attempted purchases, complete/started parent tasks, returning buyers and accepted handovers. Keep partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes in the same cohort. A result reopen, delivery retry or transport chunk continues the original result. Returning use follows a fresh period, input or customer request. Payment, full output and recovery retain separate actual clocks.

For each customer, record the previous method and, where available, the active effort and corrections of a prior execution. Compare the installed task against the same input/output definition, retaining the actual period and population so a larger later source remains visible. Record customer acceptance, incomplete coverage and unresolved corrections. Measure active implementation/support effort separately from elapsed access or review delays, and merchant receipts separately from service invoices and collected business cash.

Project and requested outcome

We are building open-source, self-hostable software for operating paid APIs, datasets and agent tools on Stellar. A merchant selects the resource and commercial terms; a buyer approves a specific request and controls its wallet and spending. The software carries that agreement through native settlement, complete usable output, fulfillment, recovery and handover to another engineer.

We request USD 38,000 for 400 prospective delivery hours over 150 days from actual award acceptance. The award will fund the remaining source, consumer and deployment engineering for two independently operated merchants and two independent buyer operators, including completion of the same useful operation through two independently operated facilitators. The delivered result will be a maintainable service on Stellar mainnet, with recurring customer use and an independently completed recovery and handover.

The existing product supplies the architecture, merchant and buyer workspaces, source adapters, payment integration, result receiving and operating controls. The six funded packages below apply that product to the selected customers’ actual sources, applications and hosts. They include installation-specific implementation and defects, provider integration, deployed threat response, production release and technical receiving.

Customer problem, need and adoption

API and data operators want to sell useful operations to applications and agents while retaining source rights, access rules and commercial control. Buyers need the complete result they approved, in a form their existing application can use. Staff also need to recover an interrupted paid request and transfer the working service to another maintainer.

That task joins four records: the approved request, the settled transfer, the delivered output and the accepted fulfillment or accounting. A payment confirmation alone does not show whether a multi-page dataset is complete, whether its values retained their original meaning, or whether an order reached its intended state. The customer’s useful task can contain several priced requests, so its aggregate cost and complete output must remain visible.

Public October 2–3 x402 reports illustrate this operational need: one merchant rejected payment-bearing requests because its POST requirement differed from a client’s GET retry; another reported settlement without its expected discovery listing. These reports concerned Base deployments, and their follow-ups include a corrected server and successful indexing. They inform the request, discovery and recovery joins we implement on Stellar.

The implementation team then takes that same task through deployment, complete result receiving, recurring use and maintainer handover.

Why Stellar and what we contribute

Stellar is the settlement layer for the approved operation. Buyer approval binds the complete request to its network, asset, recipient and integer atomic amount. The native Stellar SDK and configured payment service verify and settle the authorization; the application connects that outcome to the original source, useful result and merchant fulfillment. Buyers control signing and aggregate spending. Merchants control their resources, terms and order actions.

We compose existing ecosystem infrastructure. The x402 Exact Stellar scheme and facilitator supply payment verification and settlement. Vellar’s optional discovery extension publishes eligible settled resources to its catalogue. OpenZeppelin, Veridex and Periplo supply relevant payment infrastructure; Rumble Fish is developing facilitator, discovery and SDK capabilities. Our existing MPP Charge workbench retains that protocol’s own challenge, authorization and recovery model. We use the existing SDK and token contracts.

Our contribution is the repeated source-to-customer operation around those components: preserve the source’s types and pagination; review the exact request and terms; acquire the complete result; receive it into an existing application, report or workbook; and reopen the operating state after interruption or on another authorized host. This gives Stellar merchants a reusable path from a paid endpoint to an independently maintainable customer installation.

A retained comparison found 27 Vellar offers and two Periplo offers with no shared seller/route identity. The two-facilitator milestone therefore includes the actual registration and integration work for the same useful service. Its completion will demonstrate that a merchant can change payment infrastructure while preserving the customer operation. Reusable integration, receiving and operating improvements will return to the public source.

Defined architecture and operating behavior

The system has six components: the merchant’s private source/release workspace; its public HTTP or MCP operation; the native Stellar SDK and selected facilitator; the buyer’s private approval and spending state; complete result and delivery records; and merchant fulfillment/accounting. Node.js supplies the merchant and buyer interfaces. Source adapters and customer applications retain their own native data and operating semantics.

StageImplemented behavior
Review and publishThe merchant selects a source edition or named live query, request schema, public output, limits and resolved payment options. It reviews rights, route, network, asset, recipient, amount and authorization lifetime. Later source or terms changes become reviewed states.
Connect the sourceAdapters preserve types, missing and null values, pagination, keys, units, time basis and snapshot/live behavior. Customer-controlled credential or OAuth references select authorized access. The output identifies its source edition.
Approve and purchaseThe buyer retains the endpoint, method or MCP tool, arguments, selected terms and scope. The remote schema and challenge must match before signing. Per-payment limits and the application’s existing reservation/budget owner govern spend.
Settle and deliverThe facilitator verifies and settles the native authorization. The application retains the server outcome, complete output and durable merchant notification. Independent RPC reconciliation checks the transaction’s network, asset, parties and atomic amount.
Use and continueThe receiving application opens all pages and files required by the agreed task. Its parent acquisition retains the paid requests and incomplete coverage. Earlier acquired output remains available when a later source edition changes.
Operate and hand overThe customer selects its release, HTTPS service, restricted administration and supervision. A receiving engineer can drain, restart, roll back and restore it with the original operating history and complete customer files.

For paid MCP, the HTTP endpoint, tool and arguments remain distinct from the payment resource. An unsigned call obtains the challenge. Its full payment option, including authorization timeout, must match the saved quote before the buyer retains dispatch state and sends the signed tool call. The official MCP SDK carries payment and settlement metadata; HTTP operations use the native HTTP transport.

Recovery keeps server confirmation, independently observed transfer, complete output, receiver acknowledgment and fulfillment separately visible. An uncertain signed response retains its original dispatch state for reconciliation. Reopening an acquired result uses the saved work; an unfinished delivery continues from its original intent. A changed request or new purchase receives a new review. Export and restore carry the configuration selection, history and complete referenced files, while the receiving host supplies current authorized secret references.

The same workspaces are available through the browser, terminal, typed clients and MCP. The captured-API product connects reusable route policies to a saved operator procedure, exact native configuration review, continued publication and complete customer files. Its collaboration workflow supports independent draft edits, explicit resolution of overlapping changes and portable working-edit files. The original draft and package writers retain the save, export and receiving lifecycle. This supports installation work by multiple operators while preserving the selected source, procedures and earlier decisions.

Threat response and outcome measurement

The day-90 deliverable includes a deployment-specific threat model and monitoring plan. It assigns thresholds, notification destinations and accountable responders to the selected hosts.

The response design addresses changed requests or terms before dispatch; uncertain payment and incomplete delivery; unauthorized access to private state; observation or notification failure; and restart or local-state loss. Controls retain exact approved context, scoped authority, original financial outcomes, incomplete output and the relevant backup. Operational measures include outstanding age, useful observation coverage, alert and acknowledgment time, recovered output and restore duration. The two customer-operated response cases exercise the actual installed recovery path.

Each merchant’s output must be used by an independent buyer. A completed purchase joins a distinct approved intent, an independently observed native transfer and complete useful output. Counts deduplicate transactions within their network and each independent organization or person across agents and wallets. Reporting includes completed/attempted purchases, complete/started parent datasets or files, returning buyers, accepted handovers and the cohort’s partial, unresolved, canceled and refunded outcomes. Required fulfillment remains separately visible. Reopening an acquired result or resuming its file download continues the original purchase.

For each installation we record the existing customer task and, where available, a prior execution’s active effort, manual corrections and time to useful output. We compare the installed and recurring task against that same input/output definition, retaining the actual source population or period. Customer acceptance and unresolved corrections accompany those measurements. This assesses practical value: usable output, less manual work, repeat demand and a service the customer’s engineer can maintain.

Delivery capacity, payment timing and sustainability

SCF’s four payments would be $3,800 at award acceptance, then $7,600, $11,400 and $15,200 after the respective milestone approvals. These payment amounts differ from the cost of performing each tranche. The request is expressed in USD-equivalent value and paid in XLM using SCF’s scheduled-payment-day conversion method.

The complete resource study retains the six packages, dependencies, 400 hours and $38,000 budget. With an illustrative December 7, 2026 start and its explicit working-day calendar, 25 engineering plus eight integration/handover hours per week is the lowest examined timely allocation. All six tasks finish within their deadlines: T1 on January 6 and final handover on April 13, ahead of the illustrative May 6 day-150 target. The awarded schedule will use the actual start, named contributors and their working availability.

The selected schedule’s modeled peak additional cash requirement is $17,250 with a 14-day review/payment lag, $23,275 at 30 days and $26,600 at 60 days, under its stated labor-accrual assumptions. The opening-cash field is currently unentered. This makes the resource and payment-timing requirement explicit; the operating case records actual contributor payment commitments, receipts and work dates as they are established. Commercial proposals retain their own stages, assignments and collections.

Each tranche completion form will be submitted within 90 calendar days of receiving the previous tranche payment. Actual receipt dates set those form deadlines; the 30/90/150-day delivery plan runs from award acceptance. The same grant case retains the completed deliverables, submissions, payments and any SCF-confirmed schedule amendment.

The commercial model combines the open-source core, fixed-fee implementation of one agreed customer operation and separately scoped care. Merchants retain their resource receipts, while TokenJunkieLabs invoices its agreed engineering and handover. Our existing partner workflow researches a concrete service, prepares the complete editable implementation workshare, agrees receiving and maintenance responsibilities, and records delivery effort and collections. Eight October 12 data-platform proposals total $52,500 for 350 planned hours; these are proposed fees in their original company records. Actual acceptance, effort and support demand inform later pricing. Grant and commercial work keep their own funding assignments.

def sha(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def encoded(value):
    return (json.dumps(value, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n").encode()


def need(value, message):
    if not value:
        raise ValueError(message)


def https(value):
    parsed = urlsplit(value)
    need(parsed.scheme == "https" and parsed.hostname and not parsed.username
         and not parsed.password and not parsed.fragment, "Public HTTPS URL required")
    return value


def write_new(path, data):
    """Publish complete bytes with the original create-only contract."""
    temporary = path.with_name("." + path.name + "." + uuid.uuid4().hex + ".tmp")
    owned = False
    try:
        fd = os.open(temporary, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600)
        owned = True
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as stream:
            stream.write(data)
            stream.flush()
            os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        os.link(temporary, path, follow_symlinks=False)
        directory_fd = os.open(path.parent, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY)
        try:
            os.fsync(directory_fd)
        finally:
            os.close(directory_fd)
    finally:
        if owned:
            temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def retain_exact(path, data):
    """Reuse completed bytes directly, including on a nearly full filesystem."""
    try:
        fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        try:
            write_new(path, data)
            return
        except FileExistsError:
            fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
    with os.fdopen(fd, "rb") as stream:
        info = os.fstat(stream.fileno())
        need(stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) and not info.st_mode & 0o077
             and info.st_size == len(data), "Retained file differs: " + path.name)
        need(stream.read(len(data) + 1) == data, "Retained bytes differ: " + path.name)


@contextmanager
def output_operation(directory):
    directory.mkdir(mode=0o700, exist_ok=True)
    info = directory.lstat()
    need(stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode) and not info.st_mode & 0o077
         and info.st_uid == os.getuid(), "Use the original private output directory")
    fd = os.open(directory / ".receiving.lock",
                 os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600)
    try:
        lock_info = os.fstat(fd)
        need(stat.S_ISREG(lock_info.st_mode) and not lock_info.st_mode & 0o077,
             "Original receiving lock must be private")
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        except BlockingIOError:
            raise ValueError("The original receiving operation is already running")
        yield
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


class NoRedirect(HTTPRedirectHandler):
    def redirect_request(self, req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl):
        return None


def read_http(url, method, body=None):
    headers = {"Accept": "application/json",
               "User-Agent": "TokenJunkieLabs-Rail402-Integration/1.0"}
    if body is not None:
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    req = Request(https(url), data=body, method=method, headers=headers)
    try:
        response = build_opener(NoRedirect()).open(req, timeout=25)
    except HTTPError as error:
        response = error
    with response:
        data = response.read(MAX_CAPTURE + 1)
        need(len(data) <= MAX_CAPTURE, "Response exceeds capture limit")
        return {"url": url, "method": method,
                "retrievedAt": dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                "status": response.status,
                "headers": dict((k.lower(), v) for k, v in response.headers.items()),
                "bodyUtf8": data.decode("utf-8"), "bodySha256": sha(data)}


def select_offer(challenge, url):
    need(challenge.get("x402Version") == 2, "x402 version 2 required")
    need(challenge.get("resource", {}).get("url") == url,
         "Original challenge resource must match the requested URL exactly")
    offers = challenge.get("accepts")
    need(isinstance(offers, list) and 0 < len(offers) <= 32, "Original offers required")
    selected = []
    for index, offer in enumerate(offers):
        if (offer.get("scheme") == "exact" and offer.get("network") == NETWORK
                and offer.get("asset") == ASSET
                and offer.get("extra", {}).get("areFeesSponsored") is True):
            need(re.fullmatch(r"[1-9][0-9]*", str(offer.get("amount", ""))),
                 "Positive atomic amount required")
            need(re.fullmatch(r"[GC][A-Z2-7]{55}", str(offer.get("payTo", ""))),
                 "Stellar recipient required")
            need(type(offer.get("maxTimeoutSeconds")) is int
                 and 1 <= offer["maxTimeoutSeconds"] <= 86400,
                 "Native authorization lifetime required")
            need(offer.get("extra", {}).get("paymentFlow", "authorization") == "authorization",
                 "This receiving recipe selects authorization payment flow")
            selected.append(index)
    need(len(selected) == 1, "Exactly one sponsored exact testnet USDC offer required")
    return selected[0]


def request_method(method, body):
    need(method in ("GET", "POST"), "This receiving path uses the original GET or JSON POST")
    if method == "GET":
        need(body == b"", "A GET request has no body")
    else:
        need(0 < len(body) <= 16777216, "JSON POST requires the exact 1-byte to 16-MiB body")
        need(isinstance(json.loads(body), dict), "The selected JSON request must be an object")
    return method


def checked_http(record, url, method):
    need(record.get("url") == url and record.get("method") == method,
         "Retain the original HTTP source and method")
    need(isinstance(record.get("bodyUtf8"), str)
         and sha(record["bodyUtf8"].encode("utf-8")) == record.get("bodySha256"),
         "Original HTTP response bytes changed")
    return record


def capture(args):
    directory = Path(args.directory).absolute()
    need(directory.resolve() == directory, "Use the original unaliased capture path")
    body = Path(args.body_file).read_bytes() if args.body_file else b""
    method = request_method(args.method, body)
    source_input = {"schema": "commons.rail402.capture-input.v1",
                    "seller": args.url, "facilitator": args.facilitator, "method": method,
                    "requestBodySha256": sha(body), "requestBodyBytes": len(body)}
    with output_operation(directory):
        retain_exact(directory / "capture-input.json", encoded(source_input))
        retain_exact(directory / "request.json", body)
        supported_path = directory / "supported.http.json"
        supported_url = args.facilitator.rstrip("/") + "/supported"
        if supported_path.exists():
            supported = checked_http(json.loads(supported_path.read_bytes()), supported_url, "GET")
        else:
            supported = read_http(supported_url, "GET")
            retain_exact(supported_path, encoded(supported))
        response_path = directory / "challenge.http.json"
        if response_path.exists():
            response = checked_http(json.loads(response_path.read_bytes()), args.url, method)
            need(response.get("requestBodySha256") == sha(body)
                 and response.get("requestBodyBytes") == len(body), "Original request bytes changed")
        else:
            response = read_http(args.url, method, body if method == "POST" else None)
            response["requestBodySha256"] = sha(body)
            response["requestBodyBytes"] = len(body)
            retain_exact(response_path, encoded(response))
        return complete_capture(directory, body, supported, response, args.url,
                                args.facilitator, resume=True)


def complete_capture(directory, body, supported, response, url, facilitator, *, resume=False):
    retain = retain_exact if resume else write_new
    method = request_method(response.get("method"), body)
    checked_http(supported, facilitator.rstrip("/") + "/supported", "GET")
    checked_http(response, url, method)
    need(response.get("requestBodySha256") == sha(body)
         and response.get("requestBodyBytes") == len(body), "Original request bytes changed")
    need(supported["status"] == 200, "Facilitator supported response must be HTTP 200")
    kinds = json.loads(supported["bodyUtf8"]).get("kinds", [])
    need(any(k.get("x402Version") == 2 and k.get("scheme") == "exact"
             and k.get("network") == NETWORK
             and k.get("extra", {}).get("areFeesSponsored") is True for k in kinds),
         "Facilitator must advertise sponsored exact Stellar testnet")
    need(response["status"] == 402, "Seller must return the actual unpaid HTTP 402")
    header = response["headers"].get("payment-required", "")
    need(0 < len(header) <= 262144, "Original PAYMENT-REQUIRED header required")
    challenge_bytes = base64.b64decode(header, validate=True)
    challenge = json.loads(challenge_bytes)
    index = select_offer(challenge, url)
    retain(directory / "payment-required.json", challenge_bytes)
    # Only the envelope changes. Preserve the entire original challenge as its row.
    retain(directory / "offers.json", encoded({"resources": [challenge]}))
    names = ["request.json", "supported.http.json", "challenge.http.json",
             "payment-required.json", "offers.json"]
    manifest = {"schema": SCHEMA, "seller": url, "method": method,
                "facilitator": facilitator, "network": NETWORK,
                "capturedAt": response["retrievedAt"], "rowIndex": 0,
                "acceptIndex": index, "selectedOffer": challenge["accepts"][index],
                "files": {name: {"sha256": sha((directory / name).read_bytes()),
                                 "bytes": (directory / name).stat().st_size} for name in names}}
    retain(directory / "capture.json", encoded(manifest))
    retain(directory / "source-http.json", encoded({"schema": "commons.rail402.http-bundle.v1",
           "seller": url, "facilitator": facilitator, "method": method,
           "requestUtf8": body.decode("utf-8"), "supported": supported, "challenge": response}))
    return {"status": "ORIGINAL_HTTP_SOURCE_CAPTURED", "directory": str(directory),
            "manifestSha256": sha((directory / "capture.json").read_bytes()),
            "selectedOffer": manifest["selectedOffer"]}


def restore(args):
    bundle = json.loads(Path(args.source).read_bytes())
    need(bundle.get("schema") == "commons.rail402.http-bundle.v1",
         "Original Rail402 HTTP bundle required")
    supported, response = bundle["supported"], bundle["challenge"]
    body = bundle["requestUtf8"].encode("utf-8")
    method = request_method(bundle.get("method"), body)
    need(response["requestBodySha256"] == sha(body)
         and response["requestBodyBytes"] == len(body), "Original request bytes changed")
    need(supported["bodySha256"] == sha(supported["bodyUtf8"].encode("utf-8"))
         and response["bodySha256"] == sha(response["bodyUtf8"].encode("utf-8")),
         "Original HTTP response bytes changed")
    url, facilitator = https(bundle["seller"]), https(bundle["facilitator"])
    need(response["url"] == url and response["method"] == method
         and supported["url"] == facilitator.rstrip("/") + "/supported"
         and supported["method"] == "GET", "Original HTTP sources changed")
    directory = Path(args.directory).absolute()
    need(directory.resolve() == directory, "Use the original unaliased capture path")
    with output_operation(directory):
        retain_exact(directory / "capture-input.json", encoded({"schema": "commons.rail402.capture-input.v1",
                     "seller": url, "facilitator": facilitator, "method": method,
                     "requestBodySha256": sha(body), "requestBodyBytes": len(body)}))
        retain_exact(directory / "request.json", body)
        retain_exact(directory / "supported.http.json", encoded(supported))
        retain_exact(directory / "challenge.http.json", encoded(response))
        return complete_capture(directory, body, supported, response, url, facilitator, resume=True)


def read_capture(directory):
    root = Path(directory).resolve()
    manifest = json.loads((root / "capture.json").read_bytes())
    need(manifest.get("schema") == SCHEMA, "Original capture schema required")
    for name, expected in manifest["files"].items():
        need(Path(name).name == name, "Capture file must remain inside its directory")
        data = (root / name).read_bytes()
        need(len(data) == expected["bytes"] and sha(data) == expected["sha256"],
             "Retained source bytes changed: " + name)
    response = json.loads((root / "challenge.http.json").read_bytes())
    body = (root / "request.json").read_bytes()
    method = request_method(manifest.get("method"), body)
    checked_http(response, manifest["seller"], method)
    supported = json.loads((root / "supported.http.json").read_bytes())
    checked_http(supported, manifest["facilitator"].rstrip("/") + "/supported", "GET")
    need(response["status"] == 402 and response["requestBodySha256"] == sha(body)
         and response["requestBodyBytes"] == len(body), "Original HTTP request binding changed")
    challenge = json.loads((root / "payment-required.json").read_bytes())
    need(base64.b64decode(response["headers"]["payment-required"], validate=True)
         == (root / "payment-required.json").read_bytes(), "Original header bytes changed")
    need(json.loads((root / "offers.json").read_bytes()) == {"resources": [challenge]},
         "Native saved offer must carry the complete original challenge")
    need(challenge.get("extensions", {}).get("bazaar", {}).get("info", {}).get("input", {}).get("method", method)
         == method, "Original source method differs from its discovery contract")
    index = select_offer(challenge, manifest["seller"])
    need(index == manifest["acceptIndex"]
         and challenge["accepts"][index] == manifest["selectedOffer"],
         "Selected source terms changed")
    return root, manifest


PREPARE_REVIEW_JS = """
import {readFile} from 'node:fs/promises';
import {pathToFileURL} from 'node:url';
const {prepareReview} = await import(pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href);
const result = prepareReview(await readFile(process.argv[2]), JSON.parse(process.argv[3]));
process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({configSha256:result.configSha256,
    dataBase64:result.data.toString('base64')}));
"""


def prepare(args):
    root, manifest = read_capture(args.capture)
    checkout = Path(args.checkout).resolve()
    cli = checkout / NATIVE
    need(cli.is_file(), "Complete Commons checkout and original SF88 CLI required")
    need(re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,128}", args.intent_id), "Stable intent ID required")
    output = Path(args.directory).absolute()
    need(output.resolve() == output, "Use the original unaliased request path")
    body = (root / "request.json").read_bytes()
    review_path = output / "review.json"
    record_path = output / "preparation.json"
    with output_operation(output):
        retain_exact(output / "request.json", body)
        # The original pure preparer binds a pre-existing draft before resuming
        # around the original create-only CLI. Request/output paths stay fixed.
        selection = {"rowIndex": manifest["rowIndex"], "acceptIndex": manifest["acceptIndex"],
                     "intentId": args.intent_id, "url": manifest["seller"], "method": manifest["method"],
                     "responseOut": str(output / "merchant-result.json")}
        if manifest["method"] == "POST":
            selection.update({"bodyFile": str(output / "request.json"), "bodyBytes": len(body),
                              "bodySha256": sha(body), "headers": {"Content-Type": "application/json"}})
        derived = subprocess.run(
            [args.node, "--input-type=module", "-e", PREPARE_REVIEW_JS,
             str(cli.parent / "prepare.mjs"), str(root / "offers.json"),
             json.dumps(selection)], cwd=checkout, check=True, text=True, capture_output=True)
        expected = json.loads(derived.stdout)
        config_bytes = base64.b64decode(expected["dataBase64"], validate=True)
        need(sha(config_bytes) == expected["configSha256"], "Original preparer result changed")
        prior_record = json.loads(record_path.read_bytes()) if record_path.exists() else None
        if prior_record is not None:
            need(prior_record.get("schema") == "commons.rail402.native-preparation.v1"
                 and prior_record.get("intentId") == args.intent_id
                 and prior_record.get("sourceDirectory") == str(root)
                 and prior_record.get("captureManifestSha256") == sha((root / "capture.json").read_bytes())
                 and prior_record.get("reviewConfigSha256") == sha(config_bytes),
                 "Reopen the original preparation and its stable intent")
        native_path = output / "native-prepare.json"
        if review_path.exists():
            retain_exact(review_path, config_bytes)
            if native_path.exists():
                native_result = json.loads(native_path.read_bytes())
                need(native_result.get("configPath") == str(review_path)
                     and native_result.get("configSha256") == sha(config_bytes),
                     "Original preparation result differs")
            else:
                # This is the actual original prepareReview result after a
                # completed draft survived interruption before its stdout saved.
                native_result = {"mode": "OFFLINE_CONFIG_REOPENED",
                                 "configPath": str(review_path),
                                 "configSha256": expected["configSha256"],
                                 "intentId": args.intent_id,
                                 "sourceFileSha256": sha((root / "offers.json").read_bytes())}
                retain_exact(native_path, encoded(native_result))
        else:
            need(prior_record is None and not native_path.exists(),
                 "Restore the original reviewed configuration before continuing")
            argv = [args.node, str(cli), "--prepare", "--discovery", str(root / "offers.json"),
                    "--row", str(manifest["rowIndex"]), "--accept", str(manifest["acceptIndex"]),
                    "--intent-id", args.intent_id, "--url", manifest["seller"], "--method", manifest["method"],
                    "--response-out", str(output / "merchant-result.json"), "--out", str(review_path)]
            if manifest["method"] == "POST":
                argv.extend(["--body-file", str(output / "request.json"),
                             "--content-type", "application/json"])
            result = subprocess.run(argv, cwd=checkout, check=True, text=True, capture_output=True)
            native_result = json.loads(result.stdout)
            retain_exact(review_path, config_bytes)
            retain_exact(native_path, encoded(native_result))
        reviewed = subprocess.run(
            [args.node, str(cli), "--review", "--config", str(review_path)],
            cwd=checkout, check=True, text=True, capture_output=True)
        review = json.loads(reviewed.stdout)
        review_result = output / "native-review.json"
        if not review_result.exists():
            retain_exact(review_result, encoded(review))
        record = {"schema": "commons.rail402.native-preparation.v1",
                  "captureManifestSha256": sha((root / "capture.json").read_bytes()),
                  "checkout": str(checkout), "nativeCliSha256": sha(cli.read_bytes()),
                  "intentId": args.intent_id, "sourceDirectory": str(root),
                  "reviewConfig": str(review_path), "nativeResult": native_result,
                  "reviewConfigSha256": sha(config_bytes)}
        if prior_record is None:
            retain_exact(record_path, encoded(record))
        return {"status": "NATIVE_BUYER_REVIEW_REOPENED" if prior_record else "NATIVE_BUYER_REVIEW_PREPARED",
                "directory": str(output), "config": str(review_path),
                "intentId": args.intent_id, "nativeReview": review}


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    capt = sub.add_parser("capture", help="Retain the actual facilitator and unpaid seller response")
    capt.add_argument("--directory", required=True)
    capt.add_argument("--url", type=https, default=SELLER)
    capt.add_argument("--facilitator", type=https, default=FACILITATOR)
    capt.add_argument("--method", choices=("GET", "POST"), default="GET")
    capt.add_argument("--body-file", help="The exact original JSON POST body; omit for GET")
    prep = sub.add_parser("prepare", help="Call the original SF88 prepare and review commands")
    prep.add_argument("--capture", required=True)
    prep.add_argument("--checkout", required=True)
    prep.add_argument("--directory", required=True)
    prep.add_argument("--intent-id", required=True)
    prep.add_argument("--node", default="node")
    rest = sub.add_parser("restore", help="Receive a retained original HTTP bundle offline")
    rest.add_argument("--source", required=True)
    rest.add_argument("--directory", required=True)
    ins = sub.add_parser("inspect", help="Reopen and inspect the same retained source")
    ins.add_argument("--capture", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.command == "capture":
        result = capture(args)
    elif args.command == "prepare":
        result = prepare(args)
    elif args.command == "restore":
        result = restore(args)
    else:
        root, manifest = read_capture(args.capture)
        result = {"directory": str(root), **manifest}
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except (OSError, ValueError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as error:
        if isinstance(error, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
            print(error.stderr.strip(), file=sys.stderr)
        print(json.dumps({"error": type(error).__name__, "message": str(error),
                          "recovery": "Continue from the same retained capture and original intent."}),
              file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(1)

Prepare. Connect. Receive.
Unzip the packet and use Linux, Node.js 22.16 or later, Python 3.11 or later, and the existing Stellar Forge toolkit with its native and freighter-wallet features.

    
    
      
  1. PREPARE AND REVIEW
    Open the exact request.
    Restore the captured offer and prepare the original buyer. Replace the toolkit path with the receiving machine’s existing installation or checkout.
    node buyer.mjs prepare --toolkit /ABSOLUTE/EXISTING/TOOLKIT
node buyer.mjs review --toolkit /ABSOLUTE/EXISTING/TOOLKIT
    2. 
      
  2. INITIALIZE ONCE
    Bind the private operator.

    node buyer.mjs operator-init --toolkit /ABSOLUTE/EXISTING/TOOLKIT
node buyer.mjs wallet-prepare --toolkit /ABSOLUTE/EXISTING/TOOLKIT
    3. 
      
  3. CONNECT FREIGHTER
    Open the local wallet.
    Start the private server. Open its printed loopback URL in the browser with Freighter, select the intended testnet account, and connect.
    node buyer.mjs wallet-serve --toolkit /ABSOLUTE/EXISTING/TOOLKIT
    4. 
      
  4. EXECUTE AND REOPEN
    Receive the merchant response.
    Run execute in a second terminal. Review the original approval and sign the exact native authorization in Freighter. The request directory retains the actual merchant response and its JSON result view.
    node buyer.mjs execute --toolkit /ABSOLUTE/EXISTING/TOOLKIT

Hosting, service usage and payment charges stay on the commissioning party’s accounts.

# Receive the complete grant application in the original browser

This continuation opens the reviewed SCF application as a complete receiving
deliverable. It retains the manuscript, budget, financing companion and source
index; exercises the original economic report; records actual desktop and phone
views; and can print the full application from the original browser.

The application remains the original six-file manuscript projection. The
receiver does not change its economics, make a purchase, call a model, submit a
grant, start a server or construct a browser.

## Use the existing operation and listener

The original standalone source receiving is
**DCE4-SCF-GRANT-APPLICATION-RECEIVING-20261012**. It completed on Node 24.19.0:
82 selected source bodies matched their original Git identities before the
maintained composer and listener ran. The 67-route / 66-file browser closure
returned ten exact application/link/download responses, including the economic
report and 328,163-byte ZIP. The original listener then closed normally. The [original native completion](https://tokenjunkielabs.slack.com/archives/C0BTB4SUCP9/p1791809826697209?thread_ts=1791730220.899469) retains that actual result.

That completed source/HTTP result stays in its original journal. Add this
visual continuation to that same receiving. There is no reason to replay the
distribution build or retained grant purchase to obtain a browser.

The original source selection is standalone
[tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace PR106](https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/tjlabs-stellar-merchant-workspace/pull/106),
merge **e6a15209e5d8877ac4261f77e66eb859e035b842**. The six reviewed application
files retain the exact original public PR2133 identities.

The original owner reopens its selected listener through its existing lifecycle:

~~~sh
starforge grant-application --port 8787
~~~

Use the listener's actual printed origin. The --port 0 option requests an
available port. If the existing CoCart setup listener is already owned and
open, use /grant.html on that same origin. The original source command is:

~~~sh
node stellar-forge/developer-site/grant.mjs --port PORT
~~~

The source root passed below is the package's **source** directory: it contains
both stellar-forge/ and stellar/. It is not the outer release directory. Keep the
complete selected source rather than copying only the application HTML.

## Use an owned or dedicated review Page

The caller must own the Playwright Page for the whole continuation. Use the
original Page when available, or an ordinary dedicated review Page when the old
page or browser has closed. The complete reviewer work authorizes that fresh
visual view; old Page availability is not a prerequisite.

Open /grant.html first, with an explicit viewport, and leave the film at its
unstarted position. A page with a playing or already-started film stays with
its current viewer instead of losing that viewer's position.

The owner chooses the output directory on its already selected execution host,
and includes the page, PDF and retained-download allocation in that original
operation. The receiver adds no runtime installation.

~~~js
import { inspectGrantApplication } from
  './stellar-forge/developer-site/GRANT_RECEIVING.mjs';

// page is an owned or dedicated review Page for this original operation.
// sourceRoot is the exact selected installed source, not another checkout.
const applicationReceiving = await inspectGrantApplication(page, {
  sourceRoot,
  outputDirectory: originalApplicationVisualDirectory,
  expectedOrigin: originalGrantListenerOrigin,
  sourceCommit: actualSelectedSourceCommit,
  operationId: 'DCE4-SCF-GRANT-APPLICATION-RECEIVING-20261012',
  readPublishedFilm: true,
  printPdf: true,
});

record.application_visual_receiving = applicationReceiving;
await checkpoint();
~~~

The relative import is from a caller at the selected source root; another caller
uses its exact absolute file URL. This module imports only Node standard
libraries and the original maintained readBrowserAssets parser. The original
receiving owner supplies Playwright and its existing or freshly opened review browser. There is no top-level driver,
hidden browser launch or second controller.

The old retained-purchase managed receiver has an inspectLive callback that
closes over its existing Page. That callback can host an owner-coordinated
application inspection while the same grant listener is open, after explicitly
opening this reader on the Page and before its normal blank/cleanup step.
Do **not** invoke WORKBENCH_RECEIVING.mjs merely to obtain a browser: it owns
the complete original purchase/workbench CLI lifecycle. Its managed operation
and quote identities are a separate completed history.

A dedicated Page can be created through the original browser once its ownership
is settled:

~~~js
const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 1000 } });
try {
  await page.goto(originalGrantListenerOrigin + '/grant.html');
  // Call inspectGrantApplication as above and retain the original result.
} finally {
  await page.close();
}
~~~

If the prior browser is closed, the receiving owner may open one ordinary
review browser on the authorized host. Reopen the same selected source with
the supported grant-application server command. This does not replay the
distribution composer, purchase workbench, payment, model or submission.

## What the original reader exercises

The application portion opens all ten section anchors and keeps the full
manuscript accessible. It captures the desktop opening, funded work and
capacity/cash sections. The four actual application download controls must
return the exact selected source bytes:

| Original control | Retained output |
| --- | --- |
| Download submission answer | Application.md |
| Six-package budget | Six_Package_Budget.csv |
| Detailed product and financing companion | Product_and_Finance.md |
| Source and measure index | Source_Index.json |

At 390-pixel width it checks that the page fits the viewport and exercises a
labelled table's native keyboard scrolling. It captures the same application
and funded-work view. The original Chromium print command, when selected,
produces **SCF_Application.pdf** through the application's own A4 CSS.

With readPublishedFilm enabled, the existing player loads the actual published
product/team film's native duration and dimensions. The companion's original
download link must return a successful HEAD response, and its length is compared
when that header is returned. These are metadata/open checks; the receiver does
not claim to watch the whole 3:32 film. The movie and editable ZIP are not copied
into another local release.

The economic report uses the exact retained original source, without another
FRED fetch or calculation. The continuation opens Summary, Measures and Sources;
uses all three series and all three original source states; reads both
comparison pages; and downloads the full CSV and JSON through the actual
report buttons. It compares those bytes/data to the retained results.

The original report contains 75 selected observations and 150 comparisons:
144 available, four source-missing and two baseline-missing results. Missing
values remain distinct from zero and available measurements.

The economic HTML, complete measures/data, opening guide and original
328,163-byte source ZIP are retained with the receiving. Desktop and phone
captures include the missing-source view and original units, dates, publisher
and method. The original Site home then leads back to the same grant entry.

Finally, the receiver restores the original grant URL, scroll and explicit
viewport. Scroll restoration is nonanimated, and the actual horizontal and
vertical coordinates must return within one pixel before completion. It removes only its own page listeners and read-only route guard.
The owner retains the listener/browser lifecycle. Completion is not recorded
until the original view is restored.

## Read the completed handover

**RESULT.json** is the completion pointer in the selected output directory.
Its artifact list has byte counts and SHA-256 values. Relative artifact paths
are resolved from that output directory.

Each attempt has a retained directory. The completed attempt contains:

- **GRANT_REVIEW.html**, an ordinary local overview linking the complete documents,
  economic report and actual captured views;
- the four full application downloads and optional printed PDF;
- the original self-contained economic HTML, actual CSV/JSON downloads, opening
  guide and original complete economic source ZIP;
- nine desktop/phone captures and **Receiving_Result.json**.

Open GRANT_REVIEW.html inside that attempt directory, keeping its adjacent
files. It provides an inspectable handover without another listener or financial
run. Add that complete actual receiving directory to the original grant-reviewer
package or private review handover. Preserve the source selection and original
composer/HTTP result alongside it.

The original owner/reviewer still needs to view the PDF and screenshots.
The machine result records real source, navigation and output; it does not
invent a human visual signoff.

## Continue after interruption

The create-only selection.json binds the operation, actual source commit/root,
listener origin, all selected source hashes and the film/print choices.
A different selection cannot overwrite it.

A completed retry verifies every retained artifact and returns the original
result without repeating the browser journey. An interrupted attempt stays
under its original directory, including completed outputs and INCOMPLETE.json
when the host could write it. Reopen the same original listener and Page with
the same selected source and arguments, then call this continuation.
Only the read-only visual journey repeats. No source build, purchase, provider
request, numerical model or grant submission is replayed.

The function does not acquire or recover a host/browser lease. The original
owner resolves its actual stopped/live state before invoking it once on its
owned Page. Do not run concurrent copies against the same Page or directory.

If remote film metadata cannot load, retain the incomplete result and actual
failure. The owner can explicitly choose readPublishedFilm: false in a
**different** receiving output directory for an offline local review. That
result labels the film as source-links-only, without claiming playback.
Likewise, printPdf: false preserves the ordinary browser's print route without
claiming a generated PDF. Keep these distinctions in the handover.

## Original source and publishing boundaries

The original browser manifest and readBrowserAssets parser determine the
routes. The receiver checks the six reviewed grant Git blobs, original economic
report/CSV/JSON/guide/package manifest/ZIP, and the selected Site home.
Another application edition requires an explicit source review and receiver
update; it must not silently replace these reviewed bodies.

The complete developer-site component already belongs to the maintained
grant-reviewer contribution. The original distribution owner includes these two
additive files through that same component, preserving every other route,
command, application provider and source file.

The owner-private hosted Site remains
**appgprj_6acba66ca7a08191897b5a8c22611397**.
The original publisher with that account binding updates it. A local
listener/browser receiving is not a hosted publication or an SCF submission.
The application author and original submission owner retain the reviewed
request, funding claims and actual submission state.
